# Copilot Instructions for Jim Tcl

## Build and test

- Canonical builds start from `auto.def`/`Makefile.in`, so prefer `./configure && make` over relying on the checked-in generated `Makefile`.
- Run the full test suite with `make test`.
- Run a single test file with `./jimsh tests/array.test`.
- `make -C tests tcl` runs the `.test` files with the system `tclsh`, which is useful for Tcl-compatibility checks.
- Use `./configure --help` and `./configure --extinfo` to inspect available extensions and module/static build options before changing extension-related code.

## High-level architecture

- `jimsh.c` is the shell entrypoint: it creates an interpreter, registers core commands, initializes statically built extensions via generated `_load-static-exts.c`, and then runs the embedded `initjimsh.tcl` startup logic.
- `jim.c` is the core interpreter/runtime. Most optional command families live in `jim-*.c`; pure Tcl extensions live in `*.tcl`.
- `initjimsh.tcl` extends `auto_path` from `JIMLIB` and the executable directory, so package discovery depends on startup path setup as well as compile-time extension selection.
- `auto.def` is the source of truth for extension selection, dependencies, and whether an extension is static, optional, or module-capable. `Makefile`, `tests/Makefile`, and related build outputs are generated from it.
- Pure Tcl extensions that are linked statically are converted into generated `_name.c` sources by `make-c-ext.tcl`. Static extension init order is generated by `make-load-static-exts.tcl`, which includes explicit priorities for dependency-sensitive extensions.
- `jim-package.c` implements `package require` by searching `auto_path`/`JIM_LIBPATH`, trying `name.so` before `name.tcl`. Review that path when changing extension packaging or load behavior.
- `examples.api/` is the canonical reference for embedding Jim in a host application; use it when changing public embedding APIs or interpreter initialization flow.

## Key conventions

- Do not hand-edit generated files such as `_*.c`, `_load-static-exts.c`, `Makefile`, `tests/Makefile`, `jim-config.h`, or `jimautoconf.h`; change the `.tcl`, `.c`, `.in`, or `auto.def` inputs instead.
- New extensions follow the existing init pattern used across `jim-*.c`: expose `Jim_<name>Init()`, call `Jim_PackageProvideCheck(interp, "<name>")`, and register commands there. Subcommand-heavy commands usually use `Jim_SubCmdProc` with a `jim_subcmd_type` table.
- Tests are standalone `.test` scripts under `tests/` that source `tests/testing.tcl`. Guard optional functionality with `needs cmd ...` so the suite adapts to feature-dependent builds.
- `tests/runall.tcl` runs most tests in child interpreters, so avoid adding tests that depend on state leaking across files.
- Public C API functions and macros should be documented in `jim.h`; internal implementation details belong in the `.c` files. Follow the existing inline-header guidance there and keep Doxygen usage minimal.
- If you change or add a feature, update `jim_tcl.txt`. If you change `jimsh` CLI flags or shell behavior, keep `SYNOPSIS`, `JIMSH COMMAND INTERPRETER`, and `RECENT CHANGES` aligned.
- Follow `STYLE`: C is C89-only, indentation is 4 spaces, exported APIs use `Jim_*`, and internal helper naming follows the existing capitalized conventions.
